what_happened: After the 4.7 s handoff, the ego was in the rightmost lane of a multi-lane road at about 6 m/s. It went straight on, then drifted right across the right edge onto the dirt and vegetation shoulder. Meanwhile the route path angled left and the command changed to LEFT. The camera view was clean before the ego left the lane, so its planned path (orange) took it off the road with nothing forcing it there.

In slow, dense highway traffic with a LEFT command, the ego drifted right of the recorded path (about 2.8 m off) into the lane of grey van 13, which was moving slowly. It then ran into the van's rear: it slowed from 4.6 to 1.9 m/s while the gap closed from 13 m to 4.4 m, which was not enough to avoid contact.

The route said RIGHT, but after handoff the ego braked from 17 to 7 m/s and steered left across several lanes toward the left road edge, about 11 m off the recorded path. At 7.9 s it hit actor 32 side-on as 32 drove up in the lane next to it, and the ego was also reaching the left road boundary.

On the highway, after handoff the ego's plan veered right toward the adjacent lane, even though the command was STRAIGHT and then LEFT. The ego drifted about 1.7 m right of the recorded path and its front hit actor 3, which was traveling alongside just ahead in the right lane.

Shortly after the policy took over at 4.7 s, the ego drifted left out of its lane while slowing from about 18 to 11 m/s. Its path pointed left even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, and the human trajectory stayed to the right. By 7.1 s the ego had driven onto the landscaped median, about 7.2 m from where the human drove.

The road curved left, but the ego slowed from about 23 to 16 m/s while still planning a straight path. It ran off the right edge onto the shoulder and sidewalk, about 2.5 m from where the human drove, with no other actor involved.

After the policy took over at 4.7 s at about 33 m/s on a clear divided road, the ego drifted left across the yellow edge line and onto the left shoulder and vegetation. The route command was RIGHT and the planned path curved to the right. The ego slowed to 23 m/s but never steered back, and it went offroad about 2.2 m from the recorded trajectory with no other actors involved.

The route command was STRAIGHT and the ego was travelling at about 41 m/s on a highway. Its planned path bent left out of its lane, and it moved into the left lane where actor 5, a white SUV, was alongside. Its front corner hit that car at 6.9 s, about 1.6 m off the recorded human path, and it never slowed down.

After the 4.7s handoff on a multi-lane freeway, the policy steered left out of its lane even though the command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. It cut into the adjacent left lane and sideswiped vehicle 41, which was travelling alongside, causing a lateral collision at 6.2s about 2.6m off the recorded path.

The ego was going about 41 m/s on a highway with a STRAIGHT command and was passing a slower white SUV (actor 5) in the lane to its left. Instead of holding its lane, it drifted left about 1.6 m off the recorded path and its front hit actor 5 at 6.9 s.

The ego kept about 41 m/s in the right lane and drove past slower actor 5 in the left lane. In the recording, the human driver slowed and moved left; the ego is 27 m ahead of the human's recorded position. Replayed actor 5 moved right into the ego's lane just ahead of it, and the ego's front clipped it while the ego was steering right late, without ever braking.

After the 4.7 s handoff on a multi-lane highway, the policy changed lanes to the left even though the command was STRAIGHT and later RIGHT. Its planned path headed toward the left lanes, and by 6.2 s it had cut into the next lane and hit car 41 there with its side, about 2.2 m off the recorded path.

The route said LEFT and the recorded human moved one lane left, but the ego drifted right into the lane of a slow silver van (actor 13). It braked only gently, from 4.0 to 1.9 m/s, while the gap shrank from 8 m to 4.4 m, and its front hit the van's rear. The ego was hit from behind after that, but its own front collision came first.

In slow highway traffic with a LEFT command, the ego drifted right and away from the recorded path (the recorded car moved left) into the space behind the slow grey van (actor 13). It braked only gently, from 4.1 to 2.0 m/s, while the gap shrank from 8 m to about 4 m, and its front hit the van at 8.1 s. The rear contact came later and does not affect the at-fault front collision.

Once the policy took over on the multi-lane freeway, it planned a lane change to the right even though the route command was STRAIGHT and later LEFT. It steered into the right lane, which was occupied, and hit actor 3 alongside it with the ego's front corner at about 6.8 m/s, ending about 1.7 m off the recorded human path.

No other actors were nearby, and the camera view was clear before the failure.
